pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: KEYS: trusted: sanitize all key material commit ee618b4619b72527aaed765f0f0b74072b281159 upstream. As the previous patch did for encrypted-keys, zero sensitive any potentially sensitive data related to the "trusted" key type before it is freed. Notably, we were not zeroing the tpm_buf structures in which the actual key is stored for TPM seal and unseal, nor were we zeroing the trusted_key_payload in certain error paths. UPSTREAM: KEYS: trusted: fix writing past end of buffer in trusted_read() commit a3c812f7cfd80cf51e8f5b7034f7418f6beb56c1 upstream. When calling keyctl_read() on a key of type "trusted", if the user-supplied buffer was too small, the kernel ignored the buffer length and just wrote past the end of the buffer, potentially corrupting userspace memory. Fix it by instead returning the size required, as per the documentation for keyctl_read(). We also don't even fill the buffer at all in this case, as this is slightly easier to implement than doing a short read, and either behavior appears to be permitted. It also makes it match the behavior of the "encrypted" key type. UPSTREAM: KEYS: fix NULL pointer dereference during ASN.1 parsing [ver #2] commit 624f5ab8720b3371367327a822c267699c1823b8 upstream. syzkaller reported a NULL pointer dereference in asn1_ber_decoder(). It can be reproduced by the following command, assuming CONFIG_PKCS7_TEST_KEY=y: keyctl add pkcs7_test desc '' @s The bug is that if the data buffer is empty, an integer underflow occurs in the following check: if (unlikely(dp >= datalen - 1)) goto data_overrun_error; This results in the NULL data pointer being dereferenced. Fix it by checking for 'datalen - dp < 2' instead. Also fix the similar check for 'dp >= datalen - n' later in the same function. That one possibly could result in a buffer overread. The NULL pointer dereference was reproducible using the "pkcs7_test" key type but not the "asymmetric" key type because the "asymmetric" key type checks for a 0-length payload before calling into the ASN.1 decoder but the "pkcs7_test" key type does not. update_engine: Increase minor version to 4 This patch increases the minor version to 4. This minor version in the update engine adds support for three operations: - ZERO: For zeroing blocks without writing zero bytes. - DISCARD: For discarding blocks. - PUFFDIFF: Reduces the size of the delta payload for boards with ARC++. - BROTLI_BSDIFF: A new form of bsdiff patch that is 10-20% smaller. This patch might have consequences specially for the paygen tests in canary builds. Refer to the bug for proper handling of errors initiated from this patch if canary builds fail. Please read the bug before reverting this patch. BUG=chromium:782448 TEST=tryjob with canary build passes. cryptohome: don't rely on owned and not ready to continue init After moving the tpm pre-initialization step to the point before CanAttemptOwnership is received in CL:731857, we can no longer rely on checking if the tpm is 'owned' (i.e. some owner password, including possibly a well-known one set during pre-initialization) but not 'ready' (flag file created after successful initialization) yet. After pre-initialization, the tpm may be owned and not ready, but not have CanAttemptOwnership from Chrome yet. Delete the code that makes this check and rely on recently added persistent "can attempt ownership" flag instead. If this flag is set, Service will call AsyncTakeOwnership from its initialization. Even if the flag is lost, TpmCanAttemptOwnership will be sent to cryptohomed as a part of user login process, and trigger TPM initialization at that point (plus set the "can attempt ownership" flag itself in case the initialization is interrupted again). BUG=none TEST=unit tests; interrupt initialization, check that it continues after reboot Change-Id: If790533909db5c039377b328ad42e1789863ad42 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/759688 Commit-Ready: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Tested-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org>
